card.name: Drug name before 'at least X hours' spacing
card.fires_on: The last word of a drug name or verb (such as 'administer', 'taken') right before a spacing instruction like 'at least 2 hours before or after' another product. Seen in interaction sections about antacids, binding resins and similar products.

modes.label: End of drug name
modes.description: Final piece of a drug or product name that is the object of 'administer ... at least N hours'.
modes.example: Administer levothyroxine and ORLIST<<AT>> at least 4 hours apart

modes.label: Verb or 'taken' before interval
modes.description: The word 'taken' or the gap after 'at least' just before an hours-before-or-after instruction.
modes.example: TIVICAY or TIVICAY PD should be<< taken>> 2 hours before or 6 hours

card.writes: It suppresses 'short'-type words and promotes 'at least' and 'immediately', which fits an expected spacing phrase such as 'at least N hours'.
card.plain: It lights up when a label is about to say how many hours apart to give two medicines.
